description: Reverse-ETL sink: mirror an upstream DataFrame into QuickBooks Online Customer records. QBO has no single-call upsert -- POST /customer is used for both create and update, with behavior determined by the request body (Id + SyncToken present = sparse update; absent = create). This component queries by lookup_field first to discover the current SyncToken, then issues the appropriate create-or-update POST. Two API calls per row.

inputs.description: pandas DataFrame from an upstream asset. Each row -> one QuickBooks Customer record (upserted via lookup_field, with dotted fields_map keys building nested QBO objects like PrimaryEmailAddr.Address).

outputs.description: Dagster asset materialization with metadata (rows_created / rows_updated / rows_errored / api_requests). No downstream data -- the write side effect lands in QuickBooks.

upstream_asset_key.label: Upstream Asset Key
upstream_asset_key.description: Asset providing the DataFrame. Mutually exclusive with `source`.

source.label: Inline Source
source.description: Inline source config (sql / csv / inline). Mutually exclusive with `upstream_asset_key`.

lookup_field.label: Lookup Field
lookup_field.description: Top-level QuickBooks Customer field used to find an existing record via a query WHERE clause. MUST be present in fields_map values and must not contain a dot.

fields_map.label: Fields Map
fields_map.description: Upstream column -> QuickBooks Customer field name. Dotted keys build nested QBO objects (e.g. 'PrimaryEmailAddr.Address').

batch_size.label: Batch Size
batch_size.description: Max upstream rows per run (safety cap). No bulk endpoint -- each row costs 1 query (SyncToken discovery) + 1 write.

name: QuickBooks Customer Upsert
